headline: The NSA banned Furbys from its headquarters.
slides: Furby was the hottest toy of the holidays. About 14 million sold in 1999.
People believed Furbys recorded what you said and repeated it.
The NSA put out a 'Furbie Alert' banning them from its offices as a possible security risk.
The Washington Post broke the story. Agencies everywhere got asked about their Furby policy.
The maker said Furby couldn't record anything. It came preprogrammed with its words.
The NSA's Furby files were finally released through a records request.
sources: Sources: 404 Media (2024), NSA FOIA release on Archive.org, Washington Post (Jan 13 1999)
